text:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout of client v1.8.0 to eu-west-1 at 14:02 UTC — health metrics degrading, creating thread for ops.
incident-bot: Alert: 5xx rate for /v1/streaming increased from 0.2% -> 6.8% in last 3m; error signature: 'kv: stream reset by peer' and 'paging: token mismatch'. Pager duty: paging-oncall.
Maya Chen: on it, looking at canary hosts now. Initial hypothesis: new connection shim in client v1.8 changed header ordering; might break some long-poll streaming paths.
Julio Ramos: I'm seeing correlation with high concurrent paged list calls that use streaming fallback. Logs show repeated `RST_STREAM` from the runtime side followed by paging cursor desync.
Priya Patel: @Maya @Julio any customer-facing incidents? Support queue trending up for timeouts on large export jobs.
Customer Support: We have 3 customers_reporting: ACME, LumenHealth, and ShopGrid with elevated 504s. ACME is on Dedicated but using the new client SDK via their integration test harness.
Maya Chen: ACME's traces show partial pages returned then client retries with a new cursor; server rejects because we have strict stateless cursor validation. That sequence triggers 409s then clients interpret as stream error.
Anika Singh: Quick mitigation: can we flip the canary rollout off? Feature flag 'client-1-8-canary' is on in eu-west-1. If we kill it that should stop new clients from getting the shim.
Tom Baker: Rolling flag kill now: /admin/flags/kill?name=client-1-8-canary -> running.
deploy-bot: kill-flag request accepted, propagation started (targeting load balancers and runtime routing). Estimated 30s.
incident-bot: Notice: kill-flag applied to 67% of canary hosts. Observability: 5xx rate dropping from 6.8% -> 3.1% in 60s.
Julio Ramos: OK I also pushed a temporary ingress route rule to force connection reset retries to backoff (reduce retries). Patch:
```
# ingress rule
set connection_retry_limit 1
set stream_idle_timeout 30s
```
Maya Chen: Good. I'm still seeing intermittent paging cursor mismatch for sessions opened while the shim was active. We should run a one-off job to reconcile open cursors and surface to affected customers.
Priya Patel: I'll notify account leads for ACME and LumenHealth: telling them we've killed the canary flag, rolling back the client exposure, and working on cursor reconciliation. Draft msg ready:
"We're aware of elevated timeouts for exports and a small set of 5xxs caused by a canary client release. We've turned off the canary and are running fixes. No data loss expected. We'll follow up with ETA for full remediation."
Customer Support: Send that now, please. ACME replied: "Thanks, please keep us updated — we have a production job in progress." They're asking for ETA to finish job.
Maya Chen: ETA: we can re-run the customer job if they can pause and resume after we reconcile cursors; reconciliation should be ~10-30m depending on job size.
Anika Singh: Can we ship a targeted hotfix to the client that reorders header back-compat in 1.8.x, rather than full rollback? That would buy stability for customers who already adopted it.
Tom Baker: Hotfix would take ~45m to build + 20m for canary + 15m to validate. Given current customer impact, kill-flag + route mitigations are faster.
Julio Ramos: Agree. Continue with kill-flag + ingress rule. Start collecting a list of affected cursors. I'll open a job: `tools/reconcile_cursors --range last-10m --preview` and attach findings.
incident-bot: Job queued: reconcile_cursors-1901234567-1. Running on control-plane-2.
Maya Chen: Handoff in 30m: I'm stepping out for rotation. @Julio you'll take next on-call. I'll document what I've done in the runbook.
Julio Ramos: Acknowledged. I'll monitor error rate and customer queues. Immediate next steps:
- watch 5xx rate -> threshold 1%
- run reconcile job and escalate any customers with >10% cursor failures
- prepare rollback artifact if kill-flag doesn't stabilize within 10m
Priya Patel: Adding PS team for post-incident follow-up and to coordinate any customer retries.
eng-runtime: Noted — runtime team will investigate `RST_STREAM` root cause post-mitigation. Initial thought: our connection pooling + new shim header shaping may cause mid-stream frame misinterpretation on older kernel libs.
eng-platform: We'll keep an eye on canary pool health. If we need to fully rollback the service deploy, coordinate with release-engineering.
incident-bot: Update: 5xx rate now 0.9% (from peak 6.8%). ACME reported their in-flight job resumed after retrying once.
Customer Support: ACME: "Resumed, seeing normal throughput, thanks." LumenHealth still has a job queued, we offered to run it on their behalf while we confirm cursor state.
Maya Chen: Leaving notes: `actions_taken: kill flag, ingress retry limit, started cursor_reconcile job, notified customers.`
Julio Ramos: Running `reconcile_cursors` results: 42 cursor anomalies across 3 customers, all tied to sessions between 14:01:40-14:04:10 UTC. Will send CSV to support by EOD.
Tom Baker: Ops check: nothing else to roll back right now. If we see another spike within 15m we'll initiate a full rollout pause and rollback the client distribution.
Priya Patel: Postmortem owner assigned: @Maya and @Julio. Action items:
- prod test for header-ordering compatibility (eng-runtime)
- client hotfix revert plan and fast path (eng-platform + eng-runtime)
- improve observability: surface paging-cursor mismatches as a metric (instrumentation)
- customer communication template + reconfirmation flow (support)
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Creating incident ticket INC-1901234 and assigning oncall and owners.
Maya Chen: back online 30m later to check final state. All clear. Leaving handoff summary in thread and runbook.
Julio Ramos: Closing rotation notes: monitors stable, tickets updated, follow-ups scheduled. If anyone sees regression ping here.
support-bot: Notifying account teams and logging customer replies in support tracker.
Maya Chen: Thanks team :thumbsup:"
